design: FAMILY: continual / few-shot / meta-learning loop that re-learns as regimes shift. Three concrete instantiations, ordered by machinery: (i) MINIMAL — the 819 rule (sign of 30-day return, equal weight, H=1, `trader/config.py:93-105`) with its lookback L re-selected walk-forward from {7,14,30,60,90} by trailing-window net@21 Sharpe (yearly and monthly re-selection; a hysteresis variant that switches only on a >0.5-Sharpe trailing gain); equivalently Hedge/exp-weights over the 5 lookback books with a forgetting factor. (ii) MIDDLE — a rolling cross-sectional ridge forecaster (market-residual, vol-standardised target as in the memo §4.2) whose ESTIMATION WINDOW is itself chosen by a pre-registered quadratic-loss rule (Inoue–Jin–Rossi 2017) or by Bayesian online changepoint resets; the GP controller consumes the forecast unchanged. (iii) MAXIMAL — an X-Trend-style few-shot learner (Wood–Kessler–Roberts–Zohren 2024): CPD-segment the 273-asset PIT history into 'regimes', build a causal context set of past regimes, cross-attend from the current window to the context set, output positions; MAML over regimes is the same object with a different adapter. THE DISTINCTION THE BRIEF ASKS FOR: (a) if what adapts is the FORECASTER (ii, iii), this is alpha hunting with a shorter memory — bounded above by the rolling per-year IC ceiling, which is the memo's §4 instrument sliced by year (`lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:272-275, 304-306`); (b) if what adapts is the TACTIC/LOOKBACK SELECTOR (i), this is the tactics panel's K-arm selector with a recency prior, and its profit decomposes as Σ_k π_k μ_k + Σ_k Cov(1{k chosen}, R_k) − c·E[switch turnover] (`lore/fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:47-54`), where the first term is ≤0 on 2024–2026 for every measured arm and the whole case rests on the covariance (timing) term. In both cases the loop is an amplifier of a SECOND-ORDER forecast — a forecast of WHEN the first-order conditional-mean signal is switched on — and carries no information unless local IC is (1) nonzero in some windows and (2) persistent enough to be detected before it fades. Mechanics that are fixed by the record's own numbers: per-date cross-sectional IC has sampling SD ≈ 1/√N_eff ≈ 0.35 at the memo's N_eff≈8 (`memo:162-167`); a w-day window reads IC with SE 0.35/√w, so a 1-year window has SE ≈ 0.018 — the same size as the 0.02–0.03 target IC — and a 2σ detection of IC=0.03 needs w* ≈ (0.35/0.015)² ≈ 540 days ≈ 1.5 yr (IC=0.02: ≈ 3.4 yr). The regimes on record last 8–14 months (`trader/config.py:72-78`). In Sharpe units the same fact: the rule's per-year CIs are ≈ ±2 wide (2024 net@8 CI[−1.99,+2.10], LEDGER `898/trend-decay`), i.e. SE ≈ 1.0 per year, so a selector choosing among 5 lookbacks by trailing-1y Sharpe is choosing among draws whose noise exceeds any plausible true spread between lookbacks. 'Fast' adaptation at the IC level the goalposts require is therefore not a design choice — it is below the detection floor unless N_eff or the local IC is far larger than measured. That is the design's whole content, and the kill experiment below measures exactly the two quantities (per-year IC vs placebo; monthly-IC persistence τ) that would have to beat w* for any instantiation (i)–(iii) to carry information.
what_the_loop_learns: Learned object: a TIME PATH of parameters θ_t (forecaster weights, or lookback/tactic weights, or a regime-similarity kernel in the few-shot case) instead of a single θ. The only information θ_t can carry beyond a static direct estimator (one ridge fit, one measured IC, one GP controller) is the time-variation of the conditional mean: Var_t(IC_t) and its persistence φ (lag autocorrelation of the local IC). If IC_t is constant, θ_t is a noisier estimate of θ — Pesaran–Timmermann 2007 (optimal window under breaks includes pre-break data because the post-break-only estimate's variance dominates) and the forecast-combination puzzle (Smith–Wallis 2009: estimated weights lose to equal weights through weight-estimation variance) are the two theorems that price this. The few-shot version (iii) adds a second object — a learned nonparametric similarity between the current window and past regimes across assets — which is a kernel forecaster; 811 and 819 CAPACITY both measured nonlinear ≤ linear on these surfaces (`runs/819_single_asset/CAPACITY_RESULT.md` VERDICT: 'SIGNAL-LIMITED'; MLP train IC +0.19 vs OOS +0.04), so its incremental information is bounded by the same ceiling. WHY THE INFORMATION MIGHT EXIST IN DAILY OHLC ON KRAKEN: the trend rule's by-year Sharpe swings 2021 +1.78 → 2022 +1.07 → 2023 +1.07 → 2024 +0.04 → 2025 +0.66 → 2026H1 −1.66 (net@8, LEDGER `898/trend-decay`, line 103) and X-Trend's own motivation is an 87.4% TSMOM Sharpe deterioration 2018–2023 attributed to factor crowding — a story in which local predictability appears and is arbitraged away, i.e. IC_t with structure. WHY THE RECORD DOES NOT SHOW IT: each of those yearly Sharpes has SE ≈ 1.0, so the swing is not yet distinguished from sampling noise; the one direct nonstationarity measurement (TASK_906, minute lineage) found between-chunk variance 7.19× within-chunk but NO significant trend (slope p 0.12/0.27/0.66) and Levene rejecting while ANOVA does not — DIRECTIONLESS heteroskedasticity, which a mean-adaptive loop cannot exploit (a variance-adaptive sizer could, and that is the tactics panel's row 4, a turnover lever not an edge); the flagship literature for exploitable 'pockets' (Farmer–Schmidt–Timmermann 2023) was shown by Cakici et al. 2025 to rest on a two-sided kernel, and after the one-sided correction the pockets 'offer little help in forecasting market returns'. So the learned object's information content = Var(IC_t)·φ, and the record supplies no evidence that either factor is nonzero on the daily surface — only that the whole-window mean is ≈0 since 2024.
worth_if_ic_is_zero: Negative, not zero. With IC_t ≈ 0 in every window, θ_t tracks noise draws and every re-estimation is a re-trim. Quantified from the record: (1) the 819 lookback ENSEMBLE (equal weights over L∈{7,14,30,60,90} — the variance-minimising combination that the combination-puzzle literature says is the best case) already measured −0.16 net@8 vs single L=30 and raised turnover 0.162→0.177/day (`runs/819_single_asset/PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md` lever-attribution table); an ESTIMATED-weight or winner-take-all selector has strictly more weight variance than equal weights, so its null-world expectation is below −0.16. (2) If the selector wanders to a short lookback, turnover jumps: L=7d/H=1d 0.362/day, L=3d 0.587/day vs L=30d 0.154 (`runs/819_single_asset/RESULT.md` 1d table, :99-111); the 819 book's cost drag is 11.65%/yr at 21 bp for 0.152/day (`POWERED_RESULT.md` deployable metrics) and 0.18 Sharpe of drag ⇒ σ_book ≈ 65%/yr, so L=7 costs an extra ≈16%/yr ≈ −0.25 Sharpe purely in fees. (3) 892 measured that the standing book's maintenance re-trims are the anti-edge locus OOS (Δ −0.060/−0.062/−0.050 vs matched null, every CI < 0; entries/exits null) — a loop that refits more often produces more of exactly that. (4) A random-lookback selector null (which the kill experiment runs, 200 seeds) has expected net@21 ≈ 0 − c·switch turnover; the adaptive selector can only beat it through the covariance term, which is zero when IC is zero. Net: under the memo's load-bearing doubt the loop is worth ≈ −0.15 to −0.3 Sharpe relative to the frozen rule, and the frozen rule itself reads ≈0 since 2024.
measured_failure_mode_and_escape: THREE recorded failures bind this design; it escapes none of them mechanically, and the honest statement is what it converts them into. (A) 819 lever attribution: the adaptation layer on the same rule is SUBTRACTIVE (lookback ensemble −0.16, inverse-vol −0.06, all three −0.19; `PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md` lever table). Escape claimed by adaptive designs: selection instead of averaging, hysteresis on switches. Why that is not an escape: selection has higher variance than averaging (combination puzzle), and hysteresis is a parameter — under `pathway.md:30-31` a parameter nudge is not a structural change. The only real escape is a PRE-CONDITION, not a mechanism: the monthly-IC persistence half-life τ must exceed the detection window w* ≈ (2·0.35/IC_amp)² days. That is a measurement, which the kill experiment makes; if τ < w* the design is dead before any run. (B) 887's adaptive HOLD attractor (A −2.855% / E −9.106% / D −13.844% median return, monotone in activity, at fee 0 and slip 0; LEDGER line 97): any trailing-EV selector with a flat arm converges to flat when every arm's trailing EV ≤ 0 — which is the 2024–2026 state of every measured arm (trend 2024 +0.041, 2025 +0.663, 2026H1 −1.659 net@8; long-flat −5.221). Hedge-with-flat is 887 made explicit (`tactics_panel:52-54`). Mechanical 'escape' = remove the flat arm and force full gross — which forces trading a negative-EV book, i.e. the D arm of 887. There is no escape; the design must pre-register '>50% flat = FAIL' and accept the attractor as a verdict. (C) 875/892: the imprint recipe refit per expanding fold shows real in-window fit (+0.9914, `861/ref-rebase`) and OOS medians +0.31/+0.40/+0.41 on three folds with the floor swinging 15× (`875`, line 99) — fast refitting learned nothing that tracks the window; and the fold-5 seed spread (−3.65/−1.25/−2.96) is exactly the ≈1.4 Sharpe SE of a 6-month window, i.e. consistent with no signal plus sampling noise, not with a regime the learner missed. Escape: none available to a learner; the discriminating test is the by-year IC vs circular-shift placebo — if every year is inside the band, 875's spread is noise and adaptation speed is irrelevant.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: An adaptive loop's positions are functions of trailing data; the only bear-positive behaviour the record contains is the trend book's short leg (BEAR22 baseline +1.095 vs long-flat variant −2.471; 2026H1 −1.659 vs −5.221 — LEDGER `898/trend-decay`), and that is a forecast. A recency-weighted selector can only INHERIT bear-positivity from an arm that already has it; it cannot create a short signal, and its detection window (w* ≈ 1.5–3.4 yr at IC 0.02–0.03, or ≈1 yr in Sharpe units at SE≈1.0/yr) is the same order as the bear's length (BEAR22 = 13.7 months, `trader/config.py:74`), so it would recognise the bear regime at roughly the moment it ends. Few-shot/zero-shot transfer (X-Trend Table 2: TSMOM −0.26 vs X-Trend 0.47 on 20 unseen futures, 2018–23, at C=0) is the one published shape where the loop looks bear-robust — and it is a forecaster trained on 30 other assets' regimes, i.e. a forecast by construction.

literature.ref: Wood, Kessler, Roberts, Zohren 2024, 'Few-Shot Learning Patterns in Financial Time-Series for Trend-Following Strategies' (X-Trend), J. Financial Data Science 6(2):88-115; arXiv 2310.10500
literature.claim: Few-shot cross-attention over a CPD-segmented context set of past regimes improves a Deep Momentum Network; motivation is TSMOM decay attributed to factor crowding. The '10-fold over TSMOM' headline is TSMOM 0.23 → X-Trend 2.3-2.7, but the DMN baseline alone is already 2.27 — the few-shot increment is +18.9% (0.43 Sharpe) over a base learner, at ZERO transaction cost.
literature.numbers: Intro: conventional TSMOM risk-adjusted returns 'deteriorated by 87.4% from 2018 to 2023 compared to 1995-2000'. Table 1 (few-shot, 50 Pinnacle continuous futures, 10 seeds, vol-targeted 15%), avg annual Sharpe 2018-2023: Long 0.48, TSMOM 0.23, MACD 0.27, baseline DMN (Sharpe loss) 2.27, best X-Trend-Q 2.70 (+18.9%), X-Trend 2.65 (+16.9%); CPD segmentation of the context set adds +11.3%; COVID MDD 26% vs 34%, recovery 162 vs 254 days. Table 2 (zero-shot, 20 held-out futures) 2018-2023: TSMOM −0.26, baseline 0.14/0.16, X-Trend J-Gauss 0.47; 1995-2023: 1.44 vs TSMOM 0.61. Cost: 'For this paper we set C(i)=0 rather than assuming a cost for each asset' (eq. 2 context).

literature.ref: Wood, Roberts, Zohren 2022, 'Slow Momentum with Fast Reversion: A Trading Strategy Using Deep Learning and Changepoint Detection', JFDS 4(1):111-129; arXiv 2105.13727
literature.claim: Online Bayesian changepoint features inside a DMN let it switch between slow momentum and fast reversion; the regime-adaptation gain is concentrated in the recent period.
literature.numbers: CPD module: Sharpe +1/3 over 1995-2020, ≈ +2/3 over 2015-2020 (abstract). Cost treatment not read by me; the repo's tactics-panel explorer read the DMN family in full and recorded cost slopes −0.6..−0.8 Sharpe/bp and break-even 2-3 bp/side (`lore/fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md:55-58`), i.e. 7-10× past break-even at 21 bp.

literature.ref: Pesaran & Timmermann 2007, 'Selection of estimation window in the presence of breaks', J. Econometrics 137:134-161
literature.claim: Under structural breaks the MSFE-optimal estimation window generally INCLUDES pre-break data: the post-break-only (fast-adapting) estimate's variance exceeds the bias it removes. Fast adaptation is not free even when breaks are real.
literature.numbers: Theoretical result plus simulations; no single headline number. The bias-variance trade-off is the mechanism.

literature.ref: Inoue, Jin, Rossi 2017, 'Rolling window selection for out-of-sample forecasting with time-varying parameters', J. Econometrics 196(1):55-67
literature.claim: Data-driven window-length selection minimising the forecaster's quadratic loss is asymptotically valid and preferable to fixed 1y/3y windows when parameters are smooth functions of time — the econometric case FOR adaptive windows, and the one legitimate one-parameter form of it for a ridge refit.
literature.numbers: Asymptotic validity proof; macro applications; no return-forecast Sharpe reported in what I read.

literature.ref: Smith & Wallis 2009 (Oxford Bulletin) and Claeskens, Magnus, Vasnev, Wang 2016 (Int. J. Forecasting), the 'forecast combination puzzle'
literature.claim: Estimated 'optimal' combination weights are beaten by equal weights because weight-estimation variance dominates when true weights are near equal; Claeskens et al. show this holds treating the weights as random jointly with the forecasts. Direct analogue: 819's equal-weight lookback ensemble already lost −0.16 to a single L; an estimated-weight or winner-take-all selector is the puzzle's losing side.
literature.numbers: Qualitative theorem; the repo supplies the number (−0.16 net@8, `PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md` lever table).

literature.ref: Timmermann 2008, 'Elusive return predictability', Int. J. Forecasting 24(1):1-18
literature.claim: Return predictability is local and short-lived because investors' model search changes the DGP; most of the time forecasting models perform poorly, with short episodes of modest predictability; proposes adaptive forecast combination — and concludes the combination of short duration and weak predictability makes exploitation 'extraordinarily challenging'.
literature.numbers: No single headline number in what I read.

literature.ref: Farmer, Schmidt, Timmermann 2023, 'Pockets of Predictability', J. Finance 78:1279-1341; and Cakici, Fieberg, Neumaier, Poddig, Zaremba 2025, 'Pockets of Predictability: A Replication', J. Finance
literature.claim: FST: short-horizon US return predictability is local in time (pockets). Cakici et al.: FST's code used a TWO-SIDED kernel (in-sample), leaking future information; with the one-sided kernel the findings are 'qualitatively altered', 'invalidating most conclusions', and 'attempts to exploit such pockets — should they exist — offer little help in forecasting market returns'. This is the flagship evidence for harvestable local predictability, and it did not survive causality.
literature.numbers: Replication abstract only; FST's reply (SSRN 4717259) not read (403).

literature.ref: Wang & Lera 2026, 'Meta-learning for return prediction in shifting market regimes', J. Financial Markets 79 (SSRN 5022829)
literature.claim: Transformer-based Bayesian predictor (FinPFN) conditions cross-sectional forecasts on recent feature-return relationships; 'during regime changes, proxied by large volatility shifts, our method significantly outperforms benchmarks'.
literature.numbers: Data: daily Chinese A-shares + monthly US equities. Breakdown: PIT 273-asset true-daily panel build + one rule run = 82 s (POWERED_RESULT footer); 5 lookbacks × {yearly, monthly} selection + oracle + equal-weight ensemble + 200 random-selector nulls ≈ 250 scorer calls ≈ 20-40 min; per-date cross-sectional IC by year for {sign-30d, ridge on F1} × h∈{1,7,21} × 200 circular-shift placebos ≈ 1-3 CPU-hours (closed-form ridge on ≈760k (day,asset) rows, mostly NaN early). safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server per `.claude/rules/10-compute-allocation.md`. The 24 GB workstation GPU and the 3×24 GB (soon 64 GB) server GPUs are irrelevant to every arm. For the record only: an X-Trend-class learner (LSTM + cross-attention, 50 assets, 10 seeds) trains in hours on one 24 GB GPU and 273 assets would fit a 24 GB card with a smaller context set; 64 GB buys longer context sets and more seeds — but the family is priced dead at 21 bp (break-even 2-3 bp/side) before its zero-cost +18.9% increment is spent, so no GPU request is justified by this design.

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered, PIT 273-asset true UTC daily panel (`trader/data.py:426` builder, `read_ohlcv_daily`, dead coins retained, 819 liquidity filter), calendar years 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026H1 plus the 2024-01→2026-06 binding window. ARMS (all H=1, equal weight, sign signal, gross ≤1, i.e. `StrategyConfig` with only `lookbacks` varied): A = frozen L=30 (819 rule). B1 = walk-forward selector: at each calendar-year boundary choose L*∈{7,14,30,60,90} maximising trailing-1y net@21 Sharpe, hold for the year; B2 = same with monthly re-selection on trailing 1y; B3 = trailing-2y window; B4 = B1 with hysteresis (switch only if trailing gain > 0.5 Sharpe). C = ex-post per-year oracle best L (the ceiling of ANY lookback selector). D = equal-weight ensemble over the 5 L (819's −0.16 control, re-read PIT). N = 200 seeded random-L-per-period selectors (null distribution of net@21 by year and on the binding window). Turnover decomposition printed for every arm. CEILING/PERSISTENCE READ (the discriminator for question 3): per-date cross-sectional Spearman IC of (i) sign of 30d return and (ii) a ridge on F1 lagged returns {1,3,7,21,63}d (expanding refit each quarter, purge ≥h) against the market-residual, vol-standardised forward return at h∈{1,7,21}; report mean IC by calendar year with Newey–West SE (lag h); placebo = 200 circular shifts of the target by ≥63 days → per-year 95% band; persistence = autocorrelation of the MONTHLY mean-IC series at lags 1-6 with t-stats → τ (half-life). Compute w* = (2·σ_date/IC_amp)² from the measured σ_date (which also yields N_eff = 1/σ_date² as a by-product, closing the memo's unmeasured term). Everything pre-registered in a SPEC hashed by the 898 `preregister` mechanism before the first score is read.
kill_experiment.instrument: Unmodified `trader.backtest` scorer via `experiments/898_trend_decay/decay_harness.py:262 score_window` (proved byte-equal to `trader/backtest.py:328 window_metrics` by `test_decay_harness_898.py`); positions from `trader.strategy.positions_from_config` with a per-period `lookbacks` tuple (the only new code is the ~100-line selector wrapper and the IC/placebo module); seed 819, n_boot 2000, costs {0,3,8,21} bp, gate 21 bp; epoch stamped post-E-d, daily table current to the 899 seam, PIT frame pinned per `LEDGER.md:28-41`; hash-gated pre-registration copied from `decay_harness.py:304-356`.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: KILL-1 (no signal ⇒ adaptation irrelevant): in every year 2024, 2025, 2026H1, both estimators' IC at every h lie inside the placebo 95% band. KILL-2 (adaptation harmful, the expected outcome): on 2024-01→2026-06 the best selector arm B* ≤ A + 0.10 net@21 OR B* inside the random-selector null's 5-95% band OR B*'s turnover > A's with B* ≤ A. KILL-3 (STEP-0, no lookback selector of any kind): oracle C < +0.97 net@21 on 2024-01→2026-06 (if C < +0.56 record DEAD; if +0.56 ≤ C < +0.97 record MARGINAL-CEILING). Mandatory FAIL: any selector arm with a flat state >50% of decisions. SURVIVE (licenses one real adaptive row, not a goalpost pass): B* ≥ A + 0.30 net@21 on 2024-01→2026-06 AND B* > the null's 95th percentile AND IC outside the placebo band in ≥2 of {2024, 2025, 2026H1} for the same estimator AND monthly-IC lag-1..3 autocorrelation > 0 at t ≥ 2 AND measured τ > w*. Report all four KILL/SURVIVE conditions regardless of which fires; no metric added after the hash.
kill_experiment.cost: ≤0.5 CPU-day on gpu-server, wrapped; zero GPU; ~1 implementer session for the selector wrapper + IC/placebo module + SPEC; the PIT panel and scorer already exist (single 819 run 82 s). Kill date: 7 days from SPEC hash.

honest_odds: P(any continual/few-shot/meta-learning loop on daily Kraken OHLC clears the goalposts — PIT, unseen 2024-26H1, net@21 ≥ +0.97, ≥3 seeds, BEAR-positive) ≈ 1-2%; P(clears the PIT bar +0.56) ≈ 3-5%. P(kill experiment lands in SURVIVE) ≈ 10%; P(KILL-1, every year inside the placebo band) ≈ 60-70%; P(KILL-3, oracle below +0.97 even with hindsight-best lookback per year) ≈ 55-65%. Most probable concrete outcome: selector arms read A − 0.1 to A − 0.3 net@21 with turnover 0.17-0.25/day (reproducing 819's −0.16 with more variance), the oracle somewhere +0.5..+1.2 (selection-inflated), the selector far below the oracle, and per-year IC indistinguishable from placebo with σ_date ≈ 0.3-0.4 confirming w* ≫ any regime length. The operator's half-expectation is correct: this is another faint hope, and the arithmetic that says so (IC SE 0.35/√w vs an IC target of 0.02-0.03; per-year Sharpe SE ≈ 1.0) is the record's own numbers, not a new opinion. The reason to run the diagnostic anyway is that it costs minutes, measures N_eff (the memo's one unmeasured term) as a by-product, and settles question (3) of the brief for every future 'regime' proposal at once.
open_doubts: N_eff is the memo's estimate (5-15), unmeasured (TASK_825 parked). The detection-window arithmetic scales as 1/N_eff: at N_eff = 40 the 2σ window for IC 0.03 falls to ≈ 4 months and a monthly-refit loop becomes detectable in principle. Measure σ_date first; it is a by-product of the IC read.

TASK_906's excess dispersion (7.19× between/within) is on the MINUTE lineage with two open verification blockers; I have not seen the same measurement on the daily surface. If daily per-year dispersion is also directionless, the correct adaptation object is variance (vol-targeting / Yang–Zhang σ, tactics row 4), a turnover lever the record expects to FAIL on Sharpe — not the mean-adaptive loop analysed here.

The 898 by-year figures I cite are net@8; the by-year net@21 series lives in `runs/898_decay_trading_data.json` on gpu-server, which I did not open. The qualitative reading (no recent CI excludes zero) is stated in the LEDGER row for both tiers.

X-Trend's cost sensitivity: I verified C(i)=0 in the paper; the 21-bp death of the DMN family is inferred from the tactics-panel explorer's full read (break-even 2-3 bp/side), not from my own read of Lim–Zohren–Roberts 2019 or Wood 2022's cost tables.
Cakici et al. 2025 and the Farmer–Schmidt–Timmermann reply were read at snippet level only (both PDFs returned 403); the replication's headline sentence is quoted from the abstract.

One angle I did not design because it is a forecast, not a loop: few-shot transfer to NEW LISTINGS — the PIT universe has hundreds of listing events, and 'first 60-90 days post-listing' is a regime class with a genuinely shared structure across assets (X-Trend zero-shot is the published analogue). It is testable with a direct event-study estimator (post-listing drift IC, placebo by shifted listing dates) in CPU minutes; if it carries IC it enters the memo's §4 grid as a feature family, not as a learner.

The kill experiment's selector is a hard argmax over lookbacks; a softmax/Hedge over lookbacks with a tuned learning rate could be argued to sit between arm D and arm B. I treat that as a parameter of the same family (bounded between D's −0.16 and B), not as a separate design; a reviewer may disagree.

875's fold spread being 'consistent with sampling noise' is a plausibility argument (6-month Sharpe SE ≈ 1.4 vs observed 1.0-2.4), the same status TASK_906 assigns its own 875 reading. The by-year IC-vs-placebo read is what would make it a measurement.
